names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Αρσένιος ο εν τη Λαύρα του Κιέβου ασκήσας», with the rank word left off. No Slavonic form is recorded: saint.gr prints none.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Ο Όσιος Αρσένιος, λάτρης της εργασίας, έζησε κατά τον 14ο αιώνα μ.Χ.» The page gives no year of birth and no year of death, only that he fell asleep in peace.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026). He is a saint of the Kyiv Caves and that calendar is the one that would settle his own day; it was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Αρσένιος ο εν τη Λαύρα του Κιέβου ασκήσας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **Three Arsenii and a Cassian stand on this one day** and they are distinguished by the page's own epithets, not by any reading of mine: the Great at Canopus in 445, the Varnakovite in Phokis in 1111, the fool-for-Christ of Novgorod in 1570, and this one in the Caves of Kyiv in the fourteenth century. **None of the corpus's nine Kyiv-Caves folders is an Arsenius.** `wonderworker` is the page's own: «ο Χριστός του έδωσε το χάρισμα να επιτελεί θαύματα». No relics, no hymn, no place of burial.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
